This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed frontotemporal dementia patients consistent with behavioral-variant FTD (FTD subgroup) (I4), has adequate sample sizes (17 patients, 9 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group analyses comparing FTD and SD to controls (unpooled FTD vs controls) (I6,I7). The paper presents voxelwise, whole-brain results (BA labels and cluster reporting) and refers to tables/figures for coordinates, which satisfies acceptable reporting formats (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

Study uses FDG-PET (I3 satisfied). However it does not provide data specific to clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD (bvFTD) or Pick's disease: the FTLD group includes 13 patients with only 3 labelled as 'FTD' (not specified as bvFTD), so there is no distinct bvFTD group (I4 not met). The bvFTD-relevant subgroup size is <6 (FTD n=3), so the sample-size criterion for the target group is not met (I5 not met). The reported between-group voxelwise contrasts are for aggregated FTLD (vs subjective cognitive impairment) rather than a bvFTD group unpooled from other diagnoses, so there is no between-group contrast specific to bvFTD (I6 not met) and no whole-brain result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD sample (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and uses resting-state fMRI and DTI (I3,I4) with adequate sample sizes (bvFTD n=12; controls n=18) (I5). However, it does not report any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach): diffusion results are tract-specific (DTI/tractography) and functional results are ROI-to-ROI DMN connectivity (ROI-based) with non-significant between-group voxelwise findings. Therefore it fails to meet I6 and I7 (no between-group voxelwise coordinates/whole-brain maps for bvFTD vs controls). Because the paper reports only tract-based DTI and ROI/seed-based functional connectivity (no voxelwise VBM/fMRI/FDG-PET coordinate results), it meets exclusion criteria E6 (only ROI analyses / no whole-brain results) and E9 (reports DTI and seed/ROI FC rather than whole-brain voxelwise modalities required). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E6 and E9.

This is an empirical VBM study of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (23 patients included) with a healthy control group (20 controls). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise VBM group comparisons (two-sample t-test) showing atrophic clusters in bilateral anterior temporal lobes and additional regions, and voxelwise regression analyses relating behavioral measures to GM volume in the patient group. Imaging modality includes VBM (and FDG-PET performed in most patients). Sample sizes exceed the minimum (patients=23, controls=20). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results comparing bvFTD to controls are reported. Full text contains Introduction, Methods (including VBM preprocessing and statistics), Results (behavior and imaging) and Discussion; core article content is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and the reporting allowance I8. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used voxel-based morphometry (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with sufficient sample sizes (22 patients, 22 controls) (I5). It reports between-group voxelwise contrasts aligned to MNI space (I6) and presents results in tables/figures (I8). However, the VBM analysis was performed within a predefined fronto-subcortical region-of-interest mask rather than as an unmasked whole-brain voxelwise analysis. Therefore the paper effectively reports ROI-restricted voxelwise results and does not provide the required group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) result from the target sample, violating the whole-brain evidence requirement (I7). Exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and reports whole-brain voxelwise group comparisons (FTLD/FTD vs controls) with coordinates in standardized space (MNI) and corrected results, fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements (I6,I7,I8). The sample includes clinically diagnosed FTD (behavioral variant/frontotemporal dementia) as a distinct subgroup (FTD n=15) within FTLD (I4), with adequate group sizes (FTLD n=25 total; VBM available in 21 FTLD and 17 controls) exceeding the minimum of 6 per group (I5). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, VBM analyses and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered: this is not a review/meta-analysis, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and it does not use excluded modalities. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study includes FDG-PET imaging and reports whole-brain voxel-wise group differences for an FTD group (n=62) and specifies 48 bvFTD and 14 svPPA within that group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET used), I4 (bvFTD patients included in sample), I5 (bvFTD subgroup n=48 and controls n=73 exceed n>=6), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast results shown specifically for the bvFTD subgroup separate from other FTD variants), I7 (whole-brain results are reported for the combined FTD group rather than clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded for the review because the target group (bvFTD) is not analyzed/presented separately in whole-brain between-group contrasts.

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results comparing a clearly identified bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) group to controls in stereotactic space. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG-PET was used) and I5 (patient group size for FTD = 17, which is ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (paper reports ‘FTD’ but does not explicitly state clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD or Pick’s disease), I6 (no between-group contrast results reported as coordinates in MNI/Talairach comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no clearly reported whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result from the target sample), and I8 (no coordinate tables/figures of whole-brain results for bvFTD). Exclusion criteria applied: E6 (the study presents diagnostic accuracy and region/volume-of-interest/3D-SSP descriptions without reporting whole-brain voxelwise coordinate results). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This study used FDG-PET (I3 satisfied) and included an FTLD patient group of n=11 (I5 satisfied). However it does not report clinically labeled bvFTD/Pick’s disease explicitly (I4 not clearly met), and crucially it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to healthy controls; results are reported as regional/ROI hypometabolism counts and pattern descriptions rather than voxelwise coordinates (I6 and I7 not met). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI/regional analyses without whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because the VBM analyses were constrained to a fronto-striatal ROI mask (region-of-interest voxelwise analysis) rather than reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD sample clinically diagnosed, n=11), I5 (bvFTD n>=6 and controls n>=6), I6 (between-group contrasts reported in stereotactic space comparing bvFTD to controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (does not report at least one whole-brain, voxelwise group-level result for the target sample; analyses were ROI-restricted). Full text appears complete. Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it provides only ROI-limited voxelwise findings rather than qualifying whole-brain results required by the review.

The study is excluded because it does not use the required imaging modalities nor report whole-brain voxelwise results. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (reports only ROI/aggregate region analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results) and E9 (uses cortical thickness/volume measures via FreeSurfer rather than VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample) and I5 (patient group sizes ≥6: Part A n=18, Part B n=24). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (did not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET), I6 (no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), and I8 (no whole-brain coordinate tables/figures in defined stereotactic space). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the paper does not meet all required imaging/whole-brain criteria for inclusion.

The study is a retrospective case series of 8 patients with a clinical diagnosis of FTD and imaging evidence of brain sagging. It meets I3 (FDG-PET/SPECT was performed in 5 patients), I4 (patients were clinically diagnosed with FTD/bvFTD), and I5 (patient group N=8 ≥6). However it does NOT meet I6 (no between-group contrast vs. controls in MNI/Talairach space), and does NOT meet I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical results reported/coordinates provided). No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it lacks the required between-group, whole-brain voxelwise comparisons/coordinates required by I6 and I7.

This study reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses with whole-brain, cluster-corrected results (p < .05 FWE) and presents atrophy patterns for patient groups including a standalone bvFTD group (n=18) and healthy controls (n=37). It uses VBM as the imaging modality (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and sufficient sample sizes (I5). The manuscript reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses and brain–behavior correlations and references group-level atrophy maps for each patient group; these constitute between-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain results attributable to the bvFTD sample (I6, I7). Results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is an empirical study (not a review), it reports whole-brain VBM (not ROI-only), does not rely solely on seed-based FC/DTI/cortical thickness, and does not indicate disqualifying comorbid samples. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore, it meets all required inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

The full text reports resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) and diffusion MRI analyses; rs-fMRI (ICA/dual-regression of the DMN) satisfies imaging modality criterion (I3). The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=12) and controls (n=17), meeting I4 and I5 (both groups ≥6). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise between-group contrasts (Randomise, one-way ANCOVA and post-hoc t-tests) for DMN connectivity and TBSS-based DTI metrics; results are reported as cluster-based whole-brain findings with reference to supplement tables (acceptable per I6 and I8). Whole-brain voxelwise evidence from the target bvFTD group is clearly presented (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: this is an empirical study (not a review), reports whole-brain analyses (not ROI-only), and does not ONLY report seed-based FC, DTI, or cortical thickness (it includes whole-brain rs-fMRI ICA results). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This empirical study includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=41) and a matched control group (n=100), uses voxelwise structural MRI (VBM-derived W-scores in MNI152 space) and resting-state fMRI, and reports syndrome-specific, group-level whole-brain results comparing each syndrome (including bvFTD) to cognitively normal controls. At least one between-group contrast for bvFTD versus controls is presented (syndrome – cognitively normal whole-brain atrophy/FC maps and reconstructed FC matrices), and figures and voxelwise analyses are reported in MNI space. Sample sizes exceed the minimum of 6 per group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, non-empirical, or disallowed modalities) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is suitable for inclusion.

This study reports empirical imaging and behavioral data on clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (n=14) and age-matched controls (n=19). It includes voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses and resting-state fMRI connectivity, reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts and coordinates (e.g., ATL [-45,13,-37]; IFG [-52,2,14]) in standard space, and provides group-level results comparing bvFTD to controls. Sample sizes meet thresholds. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (reviews, ROI-only, comorbid psychiatric/other dementia confounds, non-empirical, or limited-to-seed-only methods) apply based on provided content.

This empirical study (Sun et al., 2023) reports task-based fMRI and VBM in a sample of 19 clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients and 20 healthy controls (both >6 participants). Data were normalized to MNI space and the paper reports voxel-wise whole-brain group-level contrasts (faces vs scrambles) with a significant cluster in the left caudate nucleus; searchlight SVM and voxel-wise analyses are reported and described in the text and figures. The study therefore satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: uses VBM and task-based fMRI (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD participants (I4), has adequate sample sizes (I5), reports between-group contrasts in stereotactic space (I6), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (I7) with acceptable reporting (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, includes whole-brain results, no disallowed imaging-only methods, and participant sample appears appropriate). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study includes resting-state fMRI (I3), clinically diagnosed bvFTD cases (n=35) (I4), and sufficient sample sizes for patients and controls (I5). However, it does not report voxelwise whole-brain results in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). Analyses are connectome/parcellation-based (220 regions) using network-based statistics and single-subject connectome distributions rather than voxelwise group-level contrasts with coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 (between-group contrasts reported in MNI/Talairach) and I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise result from the target bvFTD sample) are not met. This meets exclusion E6 (studies reporting only ROI/parcellation-based analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the article is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a subgroup (ALS-FTD) who met criteria for bvFTD and reports whole-brain voxelwise VBM (SPM/DARTEL) and TBSS results comparing that subgroup to controls; however the patient sample comprises individuals with ALS (a concurrent neurological disorder). This violates exclusion criterion E7 (samples with other neurological symptoms). Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting the imaging and reporting criteria.

Although this empirical study uses FDG-PET (I3) and includes a substantial number of participants with a predominant behavioral phenotype (bvFTD) meeting the sample-size requirement (I4, I5), it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach) comparing bvFTD to controls. The paper applies spectral decomposition to produce eigenbrains and conducts group-wise comparisons on eigenvalues and multivariate classification, but it does not provide voxelwise group-level statistical maps or coordinate tables that identify bvFTD-versus-control contrasts in MNI/Talairach space. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria I6 and I7. Met inclusion criteria: I3 (uses fMRI and voxel-based morphometry), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients), and I5 (bvFTD group and controls meet minimum n≥6). Not met: I6 and I7 — the voxelwise structural MRI analyses combined bvFTD and PNFA into a single group for patient vs control comparisons, and no group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast exclusively comparing bvFTD to controls in MNI/Talairach space is reported. The fMRI component was performed in healthy young adults only and does not provide bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) were triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a single-case clinical genetic case report of childhood-onset cerebellar ataxia due to a homozygous SQSTM1 mutation, not a study of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD). It does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET (violates I3); the sample does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick’s disease patients (violates I4); patient group size is N=1, below the required minimum of 6 (violates I5); no between-group contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing bvFTD to controls are reported (violates I6); and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results from a target bvFTD sample are presented (violates I7/I8). No exclusion criteria from the list are specifically met. Therefore the study does not satisfy the required inclusion criteria for this review and is excluded.

Exclusion E6 applied: the study reports VBM analyses but finds no significant whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level results and instead reports only small-volume (region-of-interest) corrected findings and voxelwise correlations within the patient groups. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients, n=22), I5 (patient and control group sizes ≥6). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrast comparing bvFTD group directly to controls—analyses focus on correlations within patients and combined patient cohorts rather than bvFTD vs controls), I7 (no significant group-level whole-brain voxelwise result reported for the target group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for whole-brain, between-group voxelwise results and must be excluded.

Excluded because the study does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise results specific to a bvFTD group (bvFTD subgroup = 5 subjects). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM used), I4 (bvFTD patients were included in the sample), I5 (overall patient group n=15 and control group n=12 meet the >=6 requirement), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/supplement). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no between-group contrast reported that compares a bvFTD-only group to controls where bvFTD is not pooled with other FTD subtypes) and I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly identified as coming from a bvFTD-only target sample). No exclusion criteria were triggered (none of E5–E9 apply). Because the meta-analysis objective targets bvFTD-specific whole-brain contrasts (unpooled bvFTD group) and this study only reports mixed-FTD contrasts or subgroup analyses where the bvFTD cell has n<6, it does not meet all required inclusion criteria for this review.

This study is excluded because its neuroimaging methods do not meet the required imaging-modality and whole-brain/voxelwise reporting criteria. Although it includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (N=10) and adequate controls for psychophysiology (meeting I4 and I5), imaging consisted of region-of-interest (FreeSurfer-derived cortical/gray matter volumes) and between-group ROI comparisons (bvFTD vs Alzheimer’s) with no voxelwise VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET analyses and no reported whole-brain coordinate-based (MNI/Talairach) contrasts from the bvFTD group. Thus exclusion criterion E6 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) is met. Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (required imaging modality), I6 (coordinate-based between-group contrasts), and I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level results). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

While the study uses VBM (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has sufficient sample sizes (I5), it does not report a between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrast comparing a bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). The reported whole-brain VBM results are across a heterogeneous patient sample and the bvFTD-specific analyses are ROI-restricted to the insula. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 are not met. No exclusion criteria from the list apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) as the imaging modality (I3); includes a clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) group (I4) with N=19 and a healthy control group (N=20), satisfying minimum sample sizes (I5); reports whole-brain, voxelwise between-group and behavioral–VBM analyses with coordinates/cluster reports in standard space (MNI) (I6, I7, I8). It is an empirical original study and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not a review, not ROI-only, not seed-based FC/DTI/cortical-thickness only, and the sample excludes comorbid psychiatric/other dementia cases). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This empirical study uses FDG-PET (I3) in a clinically diagnosed bvFTD sample (I4). The final patient group included 21 bvFTD patients and controls (≥6 each; I5). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses in standard MNI space with group comparisons (bvFTD vs controls) and regression analyses within the bvFTD group, with coordinates and FWE-corrected results (I6, I7). Results and coordinates are described in the text and figures/supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not a review/meta-analysis (not E5), it includes whole-brain results rather than ROI-only analyses (not E6), there is no indication of disqualifying psychiatric comorbidity or substance abuse in the bvFTD sample (E7 not met), it is empirical primary data (not E8), and it does not report only FC, DTI, or cortical thickness (not E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical study that reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) whole-brain analyses comparing clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients to healthy controls. The methods state VBM processing in SPM12 with normalization to MNI space and group-level voxelwise t-tests (cluster-based FWE correction) identifying regions of grey matter loss. Sample sizes meet thresholds (12 bvFTD patients, 20 controls). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results attributed to the bvFTD sample (figures and thresholded statistical images). Imaging modality (VBM), diagnostic group (bvFTD), adequate sample sizes, and voxelwise between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space are all satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is complete and the study is empirical, uses FDG-PET and includes clinically diagnosed frontal variant/bvFTD patients (n=13) and controls (n=21). It reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM results correlating autobiographical memory measures with resting FDG uptake in the fv-FTD group (i.e., group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results in stereotactic space). However, the paper does not present a between-group voxelwise contrast (bvFTD patients versus controls) reported in MNI/Talairach coordinates. Inclusion criterion I6 (at least one between-group contrast comparing bvFTD to controls in defined stereotactic space) is not met, so the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply.

This study should be excluded because it fails to meet the minimum sample-size inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM and [18F]FDG-PET imaging modalities), I4 (participants were clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD), I6 (reports between-group voxelwise contrasts in standard space with coordinates/tables), I7 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the bvFTD group), and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (patient group n=5, which is below the required minimum of 6 participants; control group n=10 meets the control requirement). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references). Because failure to meet I5 is sufficient for exclusion, the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not use an eligible imaging modality (I3 not met): it uses structural MRI volumetric/parcellation measures and SuStaIn modeling rather than VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET. It also does not report voxelwise, stereotactic (MNI/Talairach) between-group coordinate results or whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (I6 and I7 not met). The analyses are region/cluster-based volumetric comparisons (ROI-style), so exclusion criterion E6 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (bvFTD participants included) and I5 (patient and control group sizes >=6). Inclusion criteria not met: I3, I6, I7. Full text appears complete.

This study uses voxelwise structural MRI analysis (RAVENS/voxel-based methods) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients (including behavioral variant cases), and has adequate sample sizes (12 patients, 12 controls). However, the FTD group is pooled across subtypes (behavioral/executive, language variants, corticobasal), and the manuscript does not report any between-group voxelwise contrast specifically isolating a bvFTD (behavioral variant FTD) subgroup versus controls. Therefore it fails Inclusion Criterion I6 (bvFTD group not pooled with other patient groups in reported results). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal structural MRI study of familial FTLD mutation carriers using voxelwise gray matter maps and Bayesian longitudinal modeling; however it does not investigate a clinically diagnosed bvFTD (behavioral-variant FTD) patient group versus controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (VBM-style voxelwise structural MRI methods used), I5 (patient group size ≥6: 234 mutation carriers). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are genetic mutation carriers, not a clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Pick's disease patient group), I6 (no reported between-group contrast in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise result clearly reported for a bvFTD patient group). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered. Therefore the paper does not meet the review’s requirement to include clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients with between-group voxelwise comparisons and must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key imaging-analysis and sample-type requirements for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (FDG‑PET was used), I5 (patient group size = 8 ≥ 6). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participants are described as FTD but the paper does not explicitly state they are clinically diagnosed behavioral-variant FTD [bvFTD] or Pick’s disease), I6 (no reported between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space comparing a bvFTD group to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates are reported). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the paper does not present whole-brain voxelwise results; imaging is used for diagnostic/illustrative purposes rather than reporting voxelwise, coordinate-based group comparisons). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given the absence of explicit bvFTD sampling and lack of whole-brain voxelwise between-group coordinates/results, the study cannot be included in the coordinate-based meta-analysis.

This is a multi-center empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (normalized to MNI space) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts (FWE-corrected) comparing bvFTD to controls and to AD. The sample includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (final n=24) and controls (n=37), each >6 participants. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain VBM results (and TBSS DTI results) clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the imaging analyses are ROI/lobar volumetry rather than whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (patient groups exceed 6 participants: C9orf72+ n=23, GRN+ n=10). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not use VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET — uses FreeSurfer lobar volumetry and T1-hypointensity/WMSA measures), I4 (participants are genetic mutation carriers in predementia stages, not clinically diagnosed bvFTD/Picks disease patients as required), I6 (no stereotactic MNI/Talairach between-group coordinate results comparing bvFTD to controls), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given failure to satisfy key inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I6, I7) and presence of ROI-only analyses (E6), the study must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the imaging-modality and whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports ROI/volumetric analyses and no whole-brain voxelwise statistical results). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (participants clinically diagnosed with bvFTD), I5 (patient group n≥6 and control group n≥6 for imaging). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (did not use VBM, task/resting fMRI, or FDG-PET; study used structural MRI volumetry/FreeSurfer/BSI and fluid registration), I6 (no between-group contrast reported in MNI/Talairach space with coordinates), I7 (no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results identified for the target sample). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clearly defined bvFTD subgroup (n=64) and compares clinical phenotypes (including bvFTD) to healthy controls (n=32) using whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Imaging modality is VBM (I3). The sample contains clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) and the bvFTD group and controls exceed the 6-participant minimum (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results for each phenotype vs controls and specifies statistical thresholds and cluster reporting; results for bvFTD vs controls are described and illustrated (I6, I7). The manuscript references figures and supplementary material for spatial results (acceptable per I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Although coordinate tables are not embedded in the provided excerpt, the methods and references to figures/supplementary materials indicate voxelwise results in a standard space; thus the study meets inclusion criteria for this review.

The study used VBM and resting-state fMRI (I3) and included clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (7 bvFTD cases within the FTD-GRN+ group) (I4). Sample sizes meet minimums (14 patients, control groups ≥6) (I5). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results (VBM and functional maps) (I7) and presents results in figures/tables (I8). However, the critical requirement I6 is not met: the reported between-group contrasts compare a combined FTD-GRN+ group (mixing bvFTD and avPPA) to controls rather than reporting a bvFTD-only versus control whole-brain contrast. This study uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3) and includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (21 bvFTD patients) and healthy controls (46), meeting sample-size requirements (I4, I5). This study is excluded because it does not include clinically diagnosed bvFTD (I4 not met) and it does not report any between-group, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts in a standard space comparing a bvFTD patient group to controls (I6 and I7 not met). Excluded because the paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group to healthy controls in a defined stereotactic space (MNI/Talairach). This study performs voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses on a bvFTD subgroup (N=12) with comparison to healthy controls (12 for VBM; NC behavioral group N=16), reports whole-brain, voxelwise two-sample t-test contrasts and regression analyses relating IRI empathy scores to gray-matter atrophy using standardized coordinate space (SPM normalization to template), and presents voxelwise results (clusters reported and tabulated). Although the study is an empirical FDG-PET SPM study with adequate sample sizes and includes clinically diagnosed behavioural-variant FTD (bvFTD) patients (21/29), it does not present a between-group, voxelwise contrast specifically comparing a bvFTD-only group to healthy controls. This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (manual segmentation and shape analysis of caudate and putamen) using structural MRI, with no VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET voxelwise whole-brain analyses. This study uses VBM and includes adequate sample sizes (FTD n=37, controls present), but does not clearly meet key inclusion criteria for this bvFTD-focused review. This is an empirical multicenter study using resting-state fMRI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that enrolled 52 clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients and 60 matched healthy controls. This is an empirical VBM study that includes a clinically diagnosed bvFTD group (n=24) and healthy controls (n=179), both exceeding the minimum sample size. This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (I3); includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (36 bvFTD plus 20 FTD-ALS) (I4); has adequate sample sizes (56 patients, 23 healthy controls) (I5); reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts and VBM analyses performed in MNI space with coordinates provided (including supplementary material) (I6); presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results for the target sample (I7); and allows coordinates/results in supplements/figures as acceptable (I8). However, the study does not meet required sample size (fewer than 6 bvFTD patients; I5 not met), has no control group and reports no between-group voxelwise contrasts in MNI/Talairach space (I6 not met), and provides no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results from a target bvFTD sample (I7 not met). Therefore it fails multiple mandatory inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This study uses VBM and includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (16 bvFTD within 26 FTLD patients) and 21 healthy controls, and the patient and control sample sizes meet minimum thresholds. However the imaging analyses reported are voxelwise regression associations between grey matter and emotion-recognition performance within a combined FTLD cohort (and VBM was performed on FTLD patients only). The paper does not report a between-group voxelwise contrast comparing the bvFTD group (not pooled with other patient groups) to controls in standard stereotactic space, nor does it present bvFTD-specific whole-brain voxelwise results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I7 required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal, empirical study that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) (SPM2 optimized/modulated VBM) to compare MSTD (Tau +3 intron 10 mutation) patients to age- and gender-matched controls. Whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly identified as coming from the bvFTD-target sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, review/meta-analysis, methods-only, or disallowed imaging modalities) are met.

This is a two-case (n=2) multimodal case-comparison with detailed antemortem/postmortem MRI and histopathology. It does meet I4 (includes a Pick disease [FTLD-tau] patient with bvFTD features). However it does NOT meet key inclusion criteria: I3—imaging modalities are MRI (T1/T2*), not VBM, fMRI, or FDG-PET; I5—sample size is only 2 patients (<6 required); I6—no between-group coordinate-based contrasts in MNI/Talairach comparing a bvFTD group to controls (no group analysis); I7—no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported for a target patient group. No exclusion criteria from the list were triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore study must be excluded.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses VBM), I5 (patient group N=30 FTD and control N=14 meet sample size), I7 (reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses), I8 (whole-brain results presented as statistical maps/figures). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not clearly include the target diagnosis (bvFTD/Pick's) required by I4 and does not definitively provide a bvFTD-specific between-group contrast as required by I6.

This FDG-PET study includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients and meets imaging modality (I3), includes FTD (behavioral syndrome) patients (I4), and has sufficient patient numbers (I5). Therefore it does not satisfy the review’s requirement for bvFTD vs control whole-brain contrasts. Full text appears complete.

Although the study uses FDG-PET (I3), includes clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4), and has >=6 patients and >=6 controls (I5), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrast that is specific to a bvFTD-only group versus controls. The reported voxelwise maps and group analyses are performed on a mixed FTD patient sample (multiple FTD subtypes pooled), and group-level comparisons are presented mainly as ROI analyses. Therefore inclusion criteria I6 and I7 (bvFTD-only between-group voxelwise contrast and whole-brain group-level voxelwise result from the target sample) are not met. Full text appears complete. This is an empirical FDG-PET study of clinically diagnosed probable bvFTD patients (N=82) vs healthy controls (N=82) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise SPM t-maps and group-level comparisons. Imaging modality is FDG-PET (I3). The sample consists of clinically diagnosed bvFTD patients (I4) with adequate sample sizes (patients and controls ≥6; I5). The paper reports between-group voxelwise contrasts using SPM normalization and voxel-level t-maps (FWE-corrected), which satisfy reporting of between-group contrasts in a defined stereotactic space and whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I6, I7). Results are presented as voxelwise network and resting-state analyses and are clearly described in the main text (I8). No exclusion criteria (E5–E9) are met: this is not a review, not ROI-only, not non-empirical, and does not only report excluded modalities. Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This VBM study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) meets several inclusion criteria: I3 (uses VBM), I4 (includes clinically diagnosed FTD patients with early prominent behavioural features consistent with bvFTD within the sample), I5 (≥6 patients and ≥6 controls), and I8 (reports whole-brain results in tables/figures).
